name: vistaplatform_ask
description:
Ask a question about this tenant's inventory in plain words and get back the GROUNDED answer: the query-language predicate the platform wrote and ran, the rows it selected, and a summary in which every sentence cites a returned row as `[row:<asset id>]`. Sentences that cited nothing, or cited a row that was not returned, were dropped before you saw them.
PREFER THIS over composing a predicate yourself when you are not sure of the field names: the platform's translator is validated against the live catalogue and a query that does not validate is refused with diagnostics rather than guessed at. Use vistaplatform_query_assets directly when you already know the predicate you want — it is one call instead of several, and the answer is yours to summarise.
Read the result in order of authority: `query` first (the CANONICAL predicate that ran, including the default scope the platform AND-s in — repeat THAT string, not the question), then `rows`, then `text`. `provenance.model_id` names what wrote the summary; `source_kind` is always `inferred`.
ENTERPRISE, and provider-dependent. When this deployment cannot answer, the result is `{"available": false, "reason": …}` — an honest refusal naming which of edition / provider / a tenant switch is in the way, and never a fabricated answer. Treat it as "use vistaplatform_query_assets instead", not as "the inventory is empty", and do not retry.
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Ask about inventory

question.description: A question about this tenant's inventory, in plain words. Not a query-language predicate — use vistaplatform_query_assets for one of those.

name: vistaplatform_asset_facets
description:
Count assets by one or more facets over the set a query selects — the way to answer "how many, broken down by …?" without paging through rows. Returns, per requested facet, its buckets as {key, count}, plus `query`: the canonical query the counts were taken over. The counts and vistaplatform_query_assets run the SAME predicate, so a total here and a list there always describe the same set.
QUERY LANGUAGE. One line of text; adjacent terms mean AND. Operators: `:` loose/case-insensitive (substring on text fields, subtree on `class`), `=` exact, `!=`, `<` `<=` `>` `>=`, `in (a, b)`, `~ "regex"`, `field:[lo to hi]`, `*` wildcard, `exists(field)`, `not`/`-` to negate, parentheses to group. Child collections are EXISTS sub-predicates: `endpoint:(…)`, `cert:(…)`, `crypto:(…)`, `software:(…)`, `finding:(…)`, `identifier:(…)`. Dates: `now`, `now-30d`, `now+7d` (units s m h d w mo y). There is no null literal — use `exists(field)`.
FIELD NAMESPACES: bare names are first-class asset columns (class, display_name, hostname, primary_address, environment, business_unit, owner_email, support_group, site (site.region, site.group), location, region, zone, status, ownership, stale_status, source, risk, risk_score, risk_assessed_by, confidence_score, first_seen, last_seen); `attr.` a class attribute (attr.os_version); `fact.` a registered fact key (fact.os.name); `id.` an identifier kind (id.serial_number, id.mac, id.any); `tag.` a tenant tag (tag.owner). A bare name NEVER resolves to an attribute, fact, identifier or tag — the prefix is required.
EXAMPLES:
  1. environment:production class:hardware.computer.server not exists(owner_email)
     — production servers nobody owns.
  2. cert:(not_after < now+30d)
     — anything with a certificate expiring in the next 30 days.
  3. risk >= high and last_seen > now-7d
     — high or critical risk, seen in the last week.
  4. crypto:(algorithm.deprecated:true) and environment in (production, staging)
     — deprecated algorithms outside dev.
  5. risk:not_assessed and class:hardware
     — hardware NOBODY HAS SCORED. This is not `risk:informational`, which means "we looked and it scored zero". The two are different sets and neither implies the other.
A query that does not validate is REFUSED, never guessed at: the tool returns the diagnostics (code, message, byte span, suggestion) and no rows. Read them, fix the query, call again.
DEFAULT SCOPE: with no `status` term the platform adds `status:monitoring` — approved inventory only. It is a default, not a floor: name `status` yourself and it steps aside, so `status:pending_approval` reaches the approval queue and `status:archived` reaches assets that were archived or merged away. The echoed query is how you tell which happened.
NOTE ON `risk`: the risk facet bands the persisted per-asset score. Assets nobody has scored land in the not-assessed bucket rather than in the zero bucket — do not add them to "low risk".
title: Count assets by facet

facets.description: Facet names to count, 1-8 of: class, risk, status, environment, ownership, stale_status, site, region, zone, segment, owner_email, business_unit, support_group, operating_system, source, proposed_by, tag, has_findings, has_endpoints

query.description: The same query-language predicate the asset list takes. The counts describe exactly the set that query selects; empty means all of inventory.

name: vistaplatform_compare_cbom_artifacts
description: Diff two CBOM artifacts of the same tenant. Components are matched by purl/OID/fingerprint and every change is categorized as improvement, regression, drift or neutral with a one-phrase reason — ideal for answering "did our crypto posture regress since the last snapshot?". Comparison is an Enterprise capability: where it is not included the tool answers {"available": false, "reason": "edition"} (the artifacts still exist) instead of a diff.
title: Compare CBOM artifacts

base_id.description: UUID of the older (baseline) CBOM artifact

head_id.description: UUID of the newer CBOM artifact to compare against the baseline

name: vistaplatform_find_ip
description: Answer 'what holds this IP address?'. Returns one result per VRF the address appears in: the most specific Prefix containing it, the recorded IP Address (if any), what it is assigned to, and the asset that holds it (`asset.via` says how: interface, primary_ip4, primary_ip6 or oob_ip). A result with a prefix but a null ip_address and asset means 'inside an allocated block, nobody recorded it' — not 'unused'. An empty list means no prefix or address in the tenant's IPAM matches. Omit `vrf` to search every VRF.
title: Find an IP address

address.description: An IPv4 or IPv6 address. A zone or prefix length is ignored.

vrf.description: A VRF UUID, or the word global. Omit to look in every VRF.

name: vistaplatform_get_asset
description:
Fetch one asset by UUID with full detail: its class and how the class was decided (`class_source_kind` measured/declared/imported/inferred, `class_source_ref`, `class_confidence`), all of its identifiers (serial number, MAC, cloud resource id, …), all of its endpoints (address, port, transport, protocol, service), its class attributes and tags, its risk, and its crypto configurations and linked certificates. It also carries the commercial lifecycle a person declared (`purchase_date`, `warranty_start`, `warranty_end`, `purchase_cost` + `purchase_currency`, `purchase_order`, `vendor` = the seller, not the manufacturer, `support_contract`, `support_contract_end`, `installed_at`, `decommissioned_at`; null = not recorded) and a computed `lifecycle` block: `warranty_state` (active, expiring_90, expired) and `eos_state` (supported, eos_within_12m, past_eos) from `effective_end_of_support`, the earlier of the device type's and the platform's end of support, with its `source` (declared or catalogue). `unknown` means nothing is recorded — never report it as covered or supported. An empty `endpoints` array is a real answer, not a gap — an at-rest cloud resource has no endpoint at all. If the result carries `merged_into`, this id is a TOMBSTONE: the asset was merged into the one that field names, and it answers 200 with `asset_status: archived` rather than 404 so a stale id still resolves. Follow the pointer and report the survivor — never present a tombstone as live inventory.
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Get asset detail

name: vistaplatform_get_asset_history
description: The change history of one asset, newest first: what changed, who or what changed it (`source`, `actor_user_id`), and when. Use it to answer "when did this move / get re-classified / change owner?" and to date a posture change. History records what the platform observed or was told; it is not an audit log of user sessions.
title: Get asset history

name: vistaplatform_get_asset_impact
description:
What is affected if this asset changes — the blast radius. Returns the reachable assets with the hop distance of each, a per-depth breakdown, and `total`.
DIRECTION: `downstream` (the default) is the DEPENDENTS — what breaks if you take this asset down. `upstream` is what this asset itself rests on. People asking "what depends on this" want downstream.
The walk follows the NINE impact-bearing relationship types, echoed back as `types`. `connects_to` is the one exclusion: an observed network flow is not a dependency, and including it would make almost any asset's blast radius the entire tenant. Quote the answer as being over those types, not as "everything related".
Each type is walked in the direction its own meaning implies, so `downstream` of a controller lists the access points it manages and `downstream` of a virtual network lists the subnets it contains, while `downstream` of a server lists the applications that run on it. A user-declared `impacts` edge to a business service is included as the LAST hop; the walk does not continue past the service.
Only ACTIVE edges count, so an impact answer never rests on a proposal nobody has agreed to. The asset itself is excluded from its own result. Depth is 1-10, default 6. If `truncated` is true the closure hit the 500-node cap and `total` is a floor — say so rather than reporting a count as complete.
This is a read of recorded relationships, not a prediction. It can only know what has been collected or declared: an empty result means no impact-bearing edges are RECORDED, which is not the same as "nothing depends on this".
title: Get asset impact

direction.description: downstream (default) for what depends on this asset, upstream for what this asset depends on

name: vistaplatform_get_asset_interfaces
description: List one asset's interfaces in natural name order (Gi0/2 before Gi0/10). Use after vistaplatform_get_asset when the question is about a device's ports, its LAG members or its MAC addresses, or which of the device's virtual device contexts (VDOMs, vsys, VDCs, route domains) each interface belongs to (`virtual_device_contexts`). An unknown asset id returns an empty list, not an error.
title: Get an asset's interfaces

q.description: Substring of name, label or description

name: vistaplatform_get_asset_neighbourhood
description:
The graph around one asset to N hops: the assets reached and the edges between them. Use it to answer "what is this connected to" and to describe a segment's shape; use vistaplatform_get_asset_impact for "what breaks if this changes", which is a narrower and different walk.
Each node carries its SHORTEST hop count from the root, so a node reachable by several routes appears once.
CAPS ARE REAL AND MUST BE REPORTED. Depth is 1-3. At most 500 nodes and 2000 edges come back; past that the response sets `truncated: true` and still reports `total_nodes` and `total_edges` — the true sizes. When `truncated` is true you are looking at a PREFIX: say so, give the real totals, and never describe the result as the complete picture.
Active edges only unless `include_pending` is set. A pending edge is a proposal nobody has agreed to; if you include them, label them as proposals rather than as connections that exist.
title: Get asset neighbourhood

asset_id.description: UUID of the asset at the centre

depth.description: Hops from the asset, 1-3 (default 2). Larger is refused, not clamped.

include_pending.description: Also draw pending (unapproved) edges and the assets only they reach. Default false.

name: vistaplatform_get_asset_relationships
description:
The typed relationships attached to one asset — what it runs on, hosts, depends on, connects to, is a member of, manages, and is used by. Returns each edge with the PEER's summary (id, display name, class, status, strongest identifier), the provenance, the confidence, and when it was first and last seen, plus `total`.
DIRECTION AND LABEL ARE RELATIVE TO THE ASSET YOU ASKED ABOUT, not properties of the edge. An edge is stored once in its canonical direction and the reverse label is derived, so the same edge reads `runs_on` from one end and `runs` from the other. Report the `label`, which is already correct for the asset in your request.
PROVENANCE decides how much the edge is worth: `measured` was observed by a collector, `declared` was asserted by a user, `imported` came from a CMDB, `inferred` is the platform's own guess and is NOT agreed fact — an inferred edge sits `pending` until a person accepts it in Approvals. Say which when it matters.
Read `total`, not the array's length: the page stops at `limit`. Rejected edges are excluded unless you ask for `status: "rejected"` — someone decided those were wrong.
title: Get asset relationships

direction.description: out (this asset is the from end), in (it is the to end), or both (default)

offset.description: Edges to skip, for paging through total

status.description: pending, active, rejected or stale. Omit to get everything except rejected.

type.description: One relationship type: runs_on, hosted_on, virtualized_by, depends_on, connects_to, member_of, contains, manages, sends_data_to or impacts

name: vistaplatform_get_cbom_artifact
description: Fetch one CBOM artifact's metadata by UUID: scope snapshot, content hash, size, component count, data freshness and signature info. (Metadata only — download the CycloneDX document itself from the Vista Platform UI.)
title: Get CBOM artifact

name: vistaplatform_get_compliance_summary
description: Evaluate one licensed framework against the tenant's inventory: overall score, failing-control count, affected assets, per-family pass/warn/fail rollup and the per-control status list. Use vistaplatform_get_control_findings to drill into a failing control. A framework that is published but not activated for the tenant answers {"available": false, "reason": "framework_not_activated"} instead of a summary.
title: Get compliance summary

environment.description: Restrict evaluation to one environment, e.g. production

framework_id.description: UUID of the platform framework to evaluate (from vistaplatform_list_compliance_frameworks)

severity.description: Restrict to one severity: CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW

name: vistaplatform_get_control_findings
description: Drill into one compliance control: its description, rationale, evidence summary by severity, the paginated findings (each tied to a concrete subject) and any active overrides. On an embedded asset, `asset_type` is the asset's CLASS KEY from the class tree (e.g. `server`, `network_device.switch`) — resolve it with vistaplatform_list_asset_classes, and use vistaplatform_get_asset for its identifiers and endpoints. The finding's own `subject_type` is a different field: it says which KIND of object the measurement was taken on (asset or certificate), and `subject_id` is that object's id. A cryptographic-configuration measurement is taken per ASSET; the configurations it was read from are listed in `evidence.crypto_implementation_ids`, so follow those to reach them rather than reading `subject_id` as one. `producer` says which producer judged it; compliance findings also carry `control_id`. A control with no findings is not automatically a pass — check its status, because a control nothing was measured for is NOT ASSESSED.
title: Get control findings

control_id.description: UUID of the control (from vistaplatform_get_compliance_summary controls list)

framework_id.description: UUID of the framework the control belongs to

name: vistaplatform_get_object_changes
description: Show the recorded change history of ONE object (an asset, interface, prefix, IP address, VLAN, Business Unit, ...), newest first: who changed it (user or discovery source), when, what action, which fields, and the before/after images (secrets are redacted by the platform). Use `since` to ask 'what changed this week'. Answers 'who changed this prefix?' and 'when did this interface go down?'. An object with no recorded changes returns an empty list.
title: Get an object's changes

kind.description: The object noun, as a key: asset, interface, prefix, ip_address, vlan, vrf, business_unit, site, rack, ...

since.description: RFC 3339 time. Only changes at or after it, e.g. 2026-10-01T00:00:00Z

name: vistaplatform_get_pqc_readiness
description: Get the tenant's post-quantum readiness: totals of PQC-ready, quantum-safe-symmetric and needs-migration crypto implementations, broken down by algorithm family with suggested migration targets. The four categories are mutually exclusive and sum to the total; `unclassified` means the catalogue could not decide, NOT that the item is safe.
title: Get PQC readiness

name: vistaplatform_get_prefix
description: Fetch one Prefix with its place in the hierarchy: the `parent`, the direct `children`, `child_count`, `ip_count`, `utilization` and the free space (`available_prefixes`, `available_ips`). HONESTY: a prefix with no addresses is 0% utilised with a count, not unknown; a prefix flagged as a pool or mark-utilized is reported as the platform computes it, so quote `utilization` as returned rather than recomputing it from ip_count.
title: Get a prefix

available_limit.description: How many free blocks to list, 1-100 (default 10)

name: vistaplatform_get_risk_summary
description:
Get the tenant's top-line risk posture: asset counts by risk band, total crypto implementations and critical findings. Bands are the CVSS qualitative ratings ×10 (Critical ≥90, High 70-89, Medium 40-69, Low 1-39, Informational 0).
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Get risk summary

name: vistaplatform_list_asset_classes
description: The asset class taxonomy: every class with its key, parent, full dotted path, human label, description, the identifier kinds that establish identity for it, and its attribute schema. `is_fixed` distinguishes a platform class from a tenant-defined subclass. Read this BEFORE writing a `class:` term — `class:hardware` matches the whole subtree (server, switch, everything under it) while `class=server` matches that one class exactly, and the attribute schema tells you which `attr.` fields exist for a class.
title: List asset classes

name: vistaplatform_list_asset_software
description:
The software installed on one asset: product name, vendor, version, purl, CPE, licence, where the claim came from (`source_kind` measured/declared/imported/inferred, `source_ref`) and when it was first and last seen. Use it to answer "is <package> on this host?" and "what version of <library> is this running?".
AN EMPTY LIST IS NOT "NO SOFTWARE". It means nothing has enumerated software on this asset — no bill of materials uploaded, no host agent. The `sw.package_count` fact is what distinguishes "we looked and found none" from "nobody looked"; read it with vistaplatform_get_asset before reporting an empty list as a clean one.
ROWS WITH `status: removed` ARE INCLUDED by default and are not current. A removed install is one a later document did not list; its row is kept so "this library was here last month" stays answerable. Pass `status: active` for what is present now, and never count removed rows as installed.
`version` is the raw string the source wrote. `version_sort` is the normalised ordering key, and it is null when the version has no numeric component — which means a version comparison against that product has no answer rather than a false one.
title: List asset software

offset.description: Rows to skip, for paging. The result's total describes the whole match, not the page.

query.description: Case-insensitive substring matched against the product name, vendor, purl and CPE. Empty means every install on the asset.

status.description: Filter to one install status: active, stale or removed. Omit for all three.

name: vistaplatform_list_business_units
description: List the tenant's Business Units — the organisational owners that assets, prefixes and other objects are attributed to. Returns every Business Unit (the list is small and unpaged) with its id; pass an id as `business_unit_id` to vistaplatform_list_prefixes, or use `business_unit` in an asset query.
title: List business units

name: vistaplatform_list_cbom_artifacts
description: List the tenant's bill-of-materials artifacts — immutable, content-hashed CycloneDX snapshots, newest first. Each entry includes the scope it was generated from, its content hash, entry count, signing status, and its `artifact_kind`: `cbom` (cryptographic), `sbom` (software), `hbom` (hardware) or `inventory` (every asset with endpoints, relationships and open vulnerabilities). Read the kind before drawing a conclusion — an SBOM listing no certificates means it is not a CBOM, not that the tenant has none.
title: List CBOM artifacts

scope_id.description: Only artifacts generated from this scope UUID

name: vistaplatform_list_cbom_scopes
description: List the tenant's CBOM scopes — named, versioned asset-boundary predicates (e.g. All, Production) that define what a CBOM artifact includes.
title: List CBOM scopes

name: vistaplatform_list_compliance_frameworks
description: List compliance frameworks visible to the tenant: published frameworks with subscription/licensing state, plus per-framework evaluation status and scores for the frameworks the tenant is licensed for. Note: full control detail and evaluation require an active subscription to the framework.
title: List compliance frameworks

name: vistaplatform_list_interfaces
description: List network interfaces, physical and virtual, across the tenant's assets. An Interface belongs to one asset and carries its name, type, speed, enabled state, MAC addresses, LAG and parent links, 802.1Q mode and the virtual device contexts (VDOM, vsys, VDC, route domain) it belongs to (`virtual_device_contexts`, by id and name). Filter by asset_id for one device, or by mac_address to find which asset owns a MAC (the same MAC on two assets is a duplicate or a move). Returns `data` (the page) and `pagination.total` (the whole match). To see every interface of ONE asset in natural name order use vistaplatform_get_asset_interfaces. To find who holds an IP address use vistaplatform_find_ip.
title: List interfaces

asset_id.description: UUID of an asset. Omit to search interfaces across the whole estate.

enabled.description: Only administratively enabled (true) or disabled (false) interfaces

mac_address.description: A MAC address in any common notation. Matches the primary or any additional address of an interface; across assets this is an identity signal (the same MAC on two assets means a duplicate or a move).

name.description: Exact interface name, e.g. Gi0/1 or eth0

q.description: Substring of name, label or description

type.description: Interface type key, e.g. 1000base-t, virtual, lag, 10gbase-x-sfpp

name: vistaplatform_list_ip_addresses
description: List IP Addresses recorded in IPAM, with their status, DNS name and what they are assigned to. Filter by `parent` (a CIDR; pass vrf_id as well) to see the addresses of one prefix, or by `assigned_interface_id` to see an interface's addresses. This lists recorded addresses; it does not say who is using an address that was never recorded — to ask 'what holds 10.1.2.3?' use vistaplatform_find_ip.
title: List IP addresses

assigned_interface_id.description: UUID of an interface (see vistaplatform_get_asset_interfaces). Only addresses assigned to it.

parent.description: CIDR. Only addresses inside this prefix. Pass vrf_id too: containment is per VRF.

q.description: Free-text search over the address, DNS name and description

status.description: Address status filter, e.g. active, reserved, deprecated, dhcp, slaac

vrf_id.description: A VRF UUID, or the word global for the global routing table

name: vistaplatform_list_prefixes
description: List IP Prefixes (CIDR blocks) from the tenant's IPAM. A Prefix sits in one VRF (or the global table), nests under the longest prefix that contains it, and may belong to a Business Unit, a VLAN and a scope (site, location, ...). Use `parent` to walk down a block, `contains` to find the prefixes holding an address, and `vrf_id` to stay in one routing table. For utilisation, children and free space of ONE prefix use vistaplatform_get_prefix.
title: List prefixes

business_unit_id.description: UUID of a Business Unit (see vistaplatform_list_business_units)

contains.description: An IP address. Only prefixes that contain it, most specific last

parent.description: CIDR. Only prefixes strictly inside this one, e.g. 203.0.113.0/24

status.description: Prefix status filter, e.g. active, reserved, deprecated, container

vrf_id.description: A VRF UUID, or the word global for the global routing table. Omit for every VRF.

name: vistaplatform_list_vlans
description: List VLANs: VID, name, status, the VLAN group and Site they belong to. Use `vid` to find every VLAN with that 802.1Q id across groups (the same VID legitimately appears in several groups). Prefixes and interfaces reference VLANs by id.
title: List VLANs

q.description: Free-text search over the name and description

status.description: VLAN status filter, e.g. active, reserved, deprecated

name: vistaplatform_query_algorithms
description: Look up the platform's authoritative cryptographic algorithm assessments: strength, deprecation status, post-quantum classification, risk score, migration guidance and recommended alternatives. This catalog is the source of truth for whether an algorithm is considered weak or quantum-vulnerable — cite it rather than judging an algorithm yourself.
title: Query algorithm assessments

category.description: Algorithm category, e.g. symmetric, asymmetric, hash, kem, signature

deprecation_status.description: Deprecation filter, e.g. active, deprecated, forbidden

strength.description: Assessment filter: weak, acceptable, strong or recommended

name: vistaplatform_query_assets
description:

An asset is any configuration item the platform tracks — servers, network devices, cloud resources, applications, endpoints — classified into a hierarchical class tree (see vistaplatform_list_asset_classes). A bare name NEVER resolves to an attribute, fact, identifier or tag — the prefix is required.
EXAMPLES:
  1. environment:production class:hardware.computer.server not exists(owner_email)
     — production servers nobody owns.
  2. cert:(not_after < now+30d)
     — anything with a certificate expiring in the next 30 days.
  3. risk >= high and last_seen > now-7d
     — high or critical risk, seen in the last week.
  4. crypto:(algorithm.deprecated:true) and environment in (production, staging)
     — deprecated algorithms outside dev.
  5. risk:not_assessed and class:hardware
     — hardware NOBODY HAS SCORED. This is not `risk:informational`, which means "we looked and it scored zero". The two are different sets and neither implies the other.
A query that does not validate is REFUSED, never guessed at: the tool returns the diagnostics (code, message, byte span, suggestion) and no rows. Read them, fix the query, call again.

It is a default, not a floor: name `status` yourself and it steps aside, so `status:pending_approval` reaches the approval queue and `status:archived` reaches assets that were archived or merged away. The echoed query is how you tell which happened.
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Query assets

cursor.description: Opaque continuation token. Pass back the next_cursor from a previous result of this tool; do not construct one.

query.description: A query-language predicate over assets. Empty means every asset in inventory. See the tool description for the grammar and examples.

name: vistaplatform_query_certificates
description: Search the tenant's X.509 certificate inventory. Filter by expiry window, issuer, key algorithm/size or self-signed status. PEM bodies are omitted; fingerprints, subjects, validity windows and key parameters are included. To find the ASSETS behind expiring certificates instead, use vistaplatform_query_assets with `cert:(not_after < now+30d)`.
title: Query certificates

algorithm.description: Public key algorithm filter, e.g. RSA, ECDSA

expiring_days.description: Only certificates expiring within this many days

name: vistaplatform_query_crypto_configurations
description:
List the tenant's discovered cryptographic configurations (protocol, version, cipher suite, key exchange, signature and hash algorithms per asset). Paginated. A configuration's `risk_score` is the worst score of its linked catalogue algorithms.
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Query crypto configurations

name: vistaplatform_search
description:
Find assets by free text when you do not know a field to filter on — a hostname fragment, a serial number, a service name, a tag. Matches, case-insensitively and as a substring: display name, hostname, every identifier value, and tag keys and values. It matches NOTHING ELSE — not descriptions, not finding summaries — so a search cannot silently widen. This is the query language's free-text term with the text quoted for you; use vistaplatform_query_assets when you can name a field, because a field term is exact and this is not.
HONESTY: `risk_score` 0 with an EMPTY `risk_assessed_by` means NOT ASSESSED — nobody looked. 0 with a non-empty `risk_assessed_by` means assessed and clean. Never report the first as "no risk".
title: Search assets by free text
